 The upcoming slate has a lot to live up to after last week’s goal-fest, as the back-to-back champions sparkled in Manchester and Real Madrid triumphed in a manner that only the 15-time winners seemingly can.
--> The upcoming slate has a lot to live up to after last week’s goal-fest, as the back-to-back champions sparkled in Manchester and Real Madrid triumphed in a manner that only the 15-time winners seemingly can.
 A record 78 goals were scored on Matchday 2 to take the season tally up to 147 from 36 matches—an average of 4.08 goals per game. The scoring boom is taking us back to a bygone era and the formative years of the European Cup, with teams perhaps capitalizing on the lack of jeopardy facilitated by the format switch of three years ago.

Fener are celebrating their first Champions League appearance since 2008–09, seemingly boasting a roster capable of at least competing with Europe’s sub-elite.

Fener are celebrating their first Champions League appearance since 2008–09, seemingly boasting a roster capable of at least competing with Europe’s sub-elite.

 Czech giants Slavia Prague were one of the poorest league phase performers last season, and 2026–27 has started with a dramatic collapse against Lens and a defeat at debutants Sabah. There’s unlikely to be much of an improvement on their three-point showing from last term.

As a result, Liverpool are still relatively easy to play against, and Brentford had their way with them at the weekend until they were reduced to 10 men .

 The previous meeting arrived early in last season’s league phase, as Paris Saint-Germain overcame an early setback to win 2–1 in Montjuïc thanks to Gonçalo Ramos’s late strike. The Parisians are playing host this time around, and although both teams have injury concerns at fullback, expectations are sky-high for the quality of soccer that’ll be produced at a fervent Parc des Princes. 
--> The previous meeting arrived early in last season’s league phase, as Paris Saint-Germain overcame an early setback to win 2–1 in Montjuïc thanks to Gonçalo Ramos’s late strike. The Parisians are playing host this time around, and although both teams have injury concerns at fullback, expectations are sky-high for the quality of soccer that’ll be produced at a fervent Parc des Princes. 
 Barcelona are breaking records left, right and center in La Liga, threatening to romp to a third-straight title. Like their hosts, they’re playing soccer from a utopian future, but Tuesday’s trip to Paris represents a challenge unlike anything they’ve encountered this term—and Hansi Flick’s side went to “Hell” last week.
